chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about sea water — is it purifying (tahur)? He said: Yes.

key_terms.طَهُور: Tahur — the highest grade of ritual purity, water capable of purifying both itself and other things. Distinct from 'tahir' (merely pure). Sea water qualifies as tahur for wudu, ghusl, and removing najasah.
key_terms.مَاء الْبَحْر: Sea water / ocean water. Jurists debated whether the ruling extended to all large bodies of water; this hadith affirms its purifying status.

ai.seo_question: Is sea water (ocean water) tahur and valid for wudu in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: A student of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asked whether sea water is tahur — a higher grade of ritual purity that can be used for wudu and ghusl. The Imam's single-word answer 'Yes' establishes a foundational ruling of Shia jurisprudence: ocean and sea water is absolutely purifying, regardless of its vast volume. This hadith was narrated through a strong chain including the eminent Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman and Abdullah ibn Sinan, both trusted companions of Imam al-Sadiq.
